newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Jan-Feb retail sales fall 71.7 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Jan-Feb retail sales fall 71.7 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Bulgarian retail sales in the first two months of this year were a real 71.7 percent lower than a year earlier, National Statistics Institute (NSI) figures
BULGARIA RETAIL SALES JAN-FEB JAN JAN-FEB'96

"Soaring inflation in January and February strongly eroded the purchasing power of consumers, which resulted in a decline in retail sales of goods and services," an NSI official told a news conference.
Consumer prices had risen a cumulative 391.9 percent in the first two months.
Sales of foods fell a real 57.8 percent year-on-year and non-food sales declined a real 64.3 percent in the first two months, figures showed.
February monthly inflation was 242.7 percent -- the highest monthly rate recorded in Bulgaria. The previous high was 121 percent in February 1991, when Bulgaria first liberalised prices.
Food prices rose 277.3 percent in February month-on-month while prices of non-foods increased 267.5 percent.
The NSI has said retail sales volumes in billion levs would be made available quarterly from 1997.
